item.title: Why Go Is the Default Language of the Agent Era
item.description: 中文版是这篇文章的默认版本。 阅读中文版 → This English page stays available at this URL; the Chinese version is the one we maintain first. In one line: once AI drives the cost of writing code to near zero, a language’s value moves from how it reads to how it is reviewed — and every trade-off Go made in its first fifteen years sits on the review side. The two source posts landed in the same month, from different authors, different starting points, and the same conclusion.

item.title: A Research Report on the Golang Green Tea Garbage Collector
item.description: I. Executive SummaryThe Green Tea garbage collector (GC) is an experimental, memory-aware parallel marking algorithm for the Go runtime. It represents a fundamental redesign of the garbage collection process, shifting from an object-centric to a memory-block-centric approach to combat performance bottlenecks caused by poor memory locality in modern many-core systems. This report analyzes its design, performance characteristics, and strategic importance. The core finding is that Green Tea successfully addresses its primary goal: reducing GC CPU costs and improving scalability by enhancing memory access patterns.

item.title: Open source: NetHandle, a high-performance network listener for Go
item.description: NetHandleA library for building high-performance TCP servers, standing on the shoulders of Go. Repository: https://github.com/gitsrc/NetHandle Features High throughput, low resource use. A very small API surface to learn. TCP, UDP and UNIX sockets. Install1go get -u github.com/gitsrc/NetHandle Benchmarks50 threads × 10,000 requests 50 threads × 20,000 requests 100 threads × 10,000 requestsThe harness and the raw output are in the repository; the numbers above are from a single machine, so treat them as a relative comparison rather than a capacity claim.
